decisions.reason: As a multi-model sports flooring line built on established in-house capabilities with its own page, it represents substantial sunk investment and visible commitment, so management would persist despite uncertain results.

The mobile arena floor line embodies considerable development and production investment and is publicly presented, so dropping it would write off costs, though overlap with Product C raises some consolidation risk.
Although it overlaps with Product B, the investment in a multi-model line and its public presentation favor persistence, with weak arena demand during the pandemic attributable to temporary causes.
The chevron parquet is the home-page flagship central to the firm's announced trend-led direction, so dropping it would expose the strategic decision as a mistake and write off major investment.
This niche surface finish involved modest investment and little strategic commitment, making it easier to drop, but it fits the sports flooring system offer and costs little to maintain.
The oak skirting is a low-investment accessory without strategic visibility, but it complements the sports floor lines the firm is committed to, so it is likely retained alongside them.
